title: Secretary of State of Georgia

context.text: The seat is open: Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger (R) is running for governor.
Penny Brown Reynolds defeated Fulton County Commissioner Dana Barrett in the June 16 Democratic runoff; Tim Fleming defeated Vernon Jones 64.5% to 35.5% in the June 16 Republican runoff.
Atlanta News First's post-primary ballot rundown and The Green Papers list only Reynolds (D) and Fleming (R) for Secretary of State.

candidates.name: Tim Fleming
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 16 Republican runoff over Vernon Jones with 64.5%.

priorities.text: Restore trust in elections through reforms to make them 'secure, fair, transparent, and trusted,' including overseeing the request-for-proposals process for a new statewide voting system for 2028.
Fix professional licensing, returning to a system in which renewals take one business day and new licenses five days.
Improve customer service so Georgians can reach someone by phone at the office.

record.text: Served as deputy secretary of state under Brian Kemp; in his questionnaire he describes defending voter ID laws and streamlining professional licensing in that role.

candidates.researchNotes: His own account of his record comes from the Georgia Recorder candidate survey; his campaign site was not located. Asked whether Georgia's 2020 election was stolen he answered that there were 'serious irregularities' and that investigations documented 'issues and fraud in Fulton County.' No roll-call votes itemized.

candidates.name: Penny Brown Reynolds
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 16 Democratic runoff over Dana Barrett.

priorities.text: Secure, transparent, fair and accessible elections, rebuilding public trust through voter education and transparent processes.
Modernize the office for small businesses, make Georgia 'the easiest state in the region to start and grow a business,' and improve customer service.
Modernize professional licensing to cut wait times, and use regulatory authority against fraudulent licensing and elder exploitation.

candidates.researchNotes: She did not complete the Georgia Recorder runoff questionnaire; priorities are from her May 2026 voter-guide answers. Asked whether Georgia's 2020 election was stolen she answered 'No' and cited audits, recounts and reviews that confirmed the certified results. Campaign site was not loaded.
